messages:
maya: quick bakeoff summary for opal11b — ran int8, int6, and an experimental int5-merged quant on our GTN answer slice and two microbench workloads this morning. posting raw numbers and a short recommendation.
simon: nice, curious about int5. did it survive decoding?
maya: surprisingly stable in short QA but noisy in reasoning. table below (median across 3 runs).
```
Variant        | p50  | p95  | throughput tok/s | cost/token
opal11b-int8   | 120ms| 460ms| 240             | $0.00082
opal11b-int6   | 100ms| 520ms| 290             | $0.00026
opal11b-int5m  | 130ms| 680ms| 320             | $0.00015
```
andre: cost delta looks great for int5m, but p95 is scary. what about quality on GTN slice?
maya: GTN (n=1200; mix of short Q/A, multi-turn clarif, retrieval prompts): exact-match: int8=73.1%, int6=71.0% (delta -2.1), int5m=67.8% (delta -5.3). high-conf stratum (top 20% by model logit confidence): int5m only -0.8 pp vs int8.
beth: hallucination / false-assertion metric?
maya: halluc heuristic: int8=5.9%, int6=6.6%, int5m=9.8% (notable on multi-hop). error types: missing entity, invented source.
harry: any latency anomalies by prompt length?
maya: yes — int6 p50 slightly lower than int8 but p95 degrades on >1k token contexts. kv-cache helps but int5m still has higher tail.
simon: thinking about product impact — would we gate int5m at all?
andre: maybe only for high-throughput non-retrieval routes (summaries, safe completions). avoid retrieval+reasoning. also use a fallback to int8 when classifier flags "requires chain-of-thought".
maya: ops recommendation:
1) promote opal11b-int6 as cost-default for low-risk surfaces. rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100 over 3 weeks with daily EM/halluc checks.
2) hold int5m in experiment pool: enable for batched summary jobs where latency tail doesn't matter. do not expose to interactive QA.
3) add kv-cache for multi-turn product flows to recover tail for int6.
4) deploy a tiny routing classifier (<=200B param cheap model) that checks prompts for retrieval markers, numeric reasoning keywords, or >600 token length and routes those to int8.
5) add a gating flag for PMs to force int8 per route.
beth: can you share unit-econ sketch for our PM?
maya: quick back-of-envelope: avg session tokens=95, int8 cost/session=$0.078, int6=$0.024, int5m=$0.014. at 2M sessions/year: int8 spend ~ $156k, int6 ~$48k, int5m ~$28k. moving baseline int8 -> int6 saves ~$108k/yr.
simon: good. include developer risk note about int5m stability.
maya: monitoring recs: daily slice checks on three production-mirrored sets: short-qa (1k), multi-turn (1k), retrieval (500). trigger pager if EM drop >1.5pp or halluc delta >2pp vs int8 baseline.
eval-bot: scheduled nightly runs starting 2026-03-24 for the three slices. results will post to #eng-ml/quant-bakeoff.
andre: eng-platform notes: create model variants opal11b:int6-default and opal11b:int5m-experiment. add cost tags and route-policy support for classifier-based routing.
harry: any plan for user-facing explanation about possible regressions?
maya: suggest PM copy: "We plan to reduce serving cost by ~3x for many flows by switching to a lower-precision variant. We expect small quality regressions for complex retrieval and multi-hop tasks; we'll keep a safety routing policy and gradual rollout. If you surface user-impact or specific failures, we can pin that route to the high-precision model instantly."
simon: :thumbsup: can you open the rollout PR and link the playbook?
maya: will do. PR will include canary checklist, latency/p95 checks, cost dashboards, and rollback steps. posting link when ready.
and re: tiny heuristic suggestion: if prompt contains words like "sources", "cite", or has >2 distinct domain names -> route to int8. cheap and effective.
beth: sounds good. thanks for the summary.
maya: thanks team — will follow up with the playbook and the PR. :white_check_mark:
